The message, "You throw some X into the fire" appears when activated, "X" replaced with the firework you use. [[Basic fireworks]] can be purchased from [[Hildir]] for {{Item Link|Coins|50}}. Other colored fireworks are crafted by combining Basic fireworks with materials at a [[Workbench]] of any level. '''Trees''' are the primary source of wood. When destroyed, a full-grown tree will become a giant log that will fall over and collide with any objects in its path. Logs drop various types of wood, depending on the kind of tree. Stumps always drop ordinary wood.

== Types of trees ==
There are 9 types of trees.

=== [[Beech]] ===
Can be found in the [[Meadows]].

=== [[Birch]] ===
Can be found  in the [[Meadows]] and [[Plains]].

=== [[Oak]] ===
Can be found in the [[Meadows]].

=== [[Fir]] ===
Can be found in the [[Black Forest]], [[Swamp]] and [[Mountain]].

=== [[Pine]] ===
Can be found in the [[Black Forest]].

=== [[Ancient Tree]] ===
Can be found in the [[Swamp]].

=== [[Yggdrasil Shoot]] ===
Can be found in the [[Mistlands]].

=== [[Scorched Tree]] ===
Can be found in the [[Ashlands]].

=== [[Timber Tree]] ===
Can be found in the [[Deep North]].

== Growing behavior ==
Cut forests do not regrow, and naturally occurring small trees (large saplings labelled Beech, Fir, or Pine) do not grow into full sized trees.  Some have reported trees spontaneously appearing on rare occasions, but this will not replace a cut forest (and is quite rare).

It is, however, possible to plant tree saplings using the [[Cultivator]] and [[:Category:Seeds|seeds]] from some tree species. Planted saplings grow into large trees over time. A sapling will grow into a tree after a random passage of time, between 3,000 and 8,000 seconds (between 50 minutes and 2 hours 13 minutes 20 seconds, or about 1.67–4.44 in-game days). Keep in mind that some trees have a shorter maximum growth time and some have a longer minimum growth time.  For tree farms, it is recommended that you plant each sapling 4 meters apart in order to avoid overcrowding, which will eliminate some saplings as surrounding trees mature.  Spacing can be measured by placing poles along one edge of the farm for reference, with the spacing measured by temporarily placing two 2-meter beams.

Ancient trees, Yggdrasil shoots and Scorched Trees do not produce seeds and cannot be planted with the cultivator.

{{Infobox location | image = Copper Deposit.png | type = Ore Deposit | id = rock4_copper (whole)
rock4_copper_frac | source = [[Black Forest]] | resources = [[Copper Ore]], [[Stone]] | durability = 50 | tool tier = 0 | resistances = pickaxe only }} '''Copper Deposits''' are resource nodes and are found in the [[Black Forest]] biome. An [[Antler Pickaxe]] or better is required to harvest Copper ore from the deposit. == Availability == Copper Deposits can be identified by their distinct dark yellow streaks. They always have the same layout with 138 nodes which extend deep underground, and each node has 50 health. When mined, the nodes yield both [[Copper Ore]] and [[Stone]]. == Drops == Each node can drop: {{loot table| {{loot row|item=Copper Ore|amt=2-4|rate=33.3%}} {{loot row|item=Stone|amt=2-4|rate=66.7%}} }} The average node, once 90% of its segments are mined, will yield about 117 {{Item link|Copper Ore|nolink=yes}} and about 234 {{Item link|Stone|nolink=yes}}. (90% was chosen to reflect how a few of the nodes will often be buried too deep to be able to be mined.) == Notes == * Metal deposits do not respawn. * Like other metals, Copper ore cannot be teleported. * Deposits overlap with the terrain, which may make them appear fully mined. However, they always extend down to the eight-meter dig limit. ** Digging down to the dig limit and then mining horizontally allows removing all the terrain in a single hit. * About 10% of the nodes will be under the dig limit and cannot be minedFully mining 10 deposits resulted in 8, 9, 11, 14, 14, 15, 15, 16, 20 and 21 nodes being under the dig limit. This is 11% of the nodes on average.. The exact amount depends on the shape of the terrain. * Deposits near water level may have most of the nodes under the water. * Nodes automatically get destroyed if they are not supported by other nodes, terrain, trees, etc. ** Entire deposits can be collapsed by digging under and around the deposit until the remaining nodes float in the air. * Support is only checked when a node is destroyed and is approximated by axis aligned bounding boxes. ** This can make it difficult to get the deposit to collapse because bounding boxes can be significantly bigger than the actual nodes and get supported even when not touching anything. * Surface level layers tend to give more Copper than the lowest dig limit area layer. * [[Troll]]s can damage and destroy Copper Deposits by attacking the player and hitting the node instead, allowing players to obtain Copper ore without a pickaxe. However, this is quite a risky method and would require the player to Dodge roll at the right moment. == Gallery == File:Copper Vein Underneath.png File:Excavated GIF.gif File:Unexcavated Copper.png File:Copper_Tree.jpg|Bounding box colliding with a tree, which prevents the deposit from collapsing (visualized with a mod). Bonfires are [[Player base|base]] structures used for cooking, sleeping and warmth.

Compared to [[Campfire]]s, they provide fire over a larger area and do not go out during rain.
== Notes ==
* Bonfires can only be placed on the ground and on stone structures.
* Multiple [[Cooking Station]]s can be placed around the Bonfire, however, the [[Cauldron]] does not work as it needs the fire directly underneath it.
* A Bonfire must be fueled with [[Wood]] in order to function. Unlike the [[Campfire]], it requires fueling with Wood immediately after placement in order to burn.
* With 1/10 fuel, a Bonfire will last for roughly 1 hour and 23 minutes. At maximum capacity, a Bonfire should burn for roughly 13 hours and 53 minutes. This duration is the same for the [[Campfire]].
* Bonfires in captured [[Fuling Village]]s can be recycled for their materials, including the [[Surtling Core]], if a Workbench is built in their vicinity.
* When exposed to rain without roof or strong wind without 70% [[cover]], the fire gets dimmer and the [[Fire Effect]] radius drops from 15 meters to 12 meters.
* Active bonfires create [[smoke]].
* Using a [[Surtling Core]] or [[Black Core]] on a bonfire produces a firework-like effect, that is visible to players outside the normal render distance.
* One of the few base structures that is not a priority target for creatures.

The '''Branch''' is an early game [[:Category:Materials|Resource]] that can be commonly found on the ground within the [[Meadows]] and [[Black Forest]] biomes.

When interacted with, the branch will be picked up providing the player one [[Wood]].

Branches will naturally respawn 4 hours after being picked.

'''Tools''' are items used to extend the player's ability to modify features of the surrounding environment (e.g. [[Tools#Building|terraforming]]) or help them accomplish a particular task (e.g. [[Tools#Adventuring|drinking]], [[Tools#Mining (Pickaxes)|mining]]).

=== Adventuring ===
* {{Item link|Tankard}} – Is used as a shortcut for consuming mead.
* {{Item link|Horn of Celebration}} – Is the same as the [[Tankard]].
* {{Item link|Dvergr Tankard}} – Is also the same as the [[Tankard]].
* {{Item link|Torch}} – Is a useful light source that can also deal fire damage, but degrades over time and cannot be repaired.
* {{Item link|Dvergr Lantern}} – Can provide light and does not degrade, but cannot really be used as a weapon.

=== Building === 
* {{Item link|Hammer}} – Is used for placing and repairing objects.
* {{Item link|Hoe}} – Can be used to flatten/raise terrain and create paths/roads.
* {{Item link|Serving Tray}} – Can be used to place [[Food]] and [[Feast]].

=== Farming ===
* {{Item link|Cultivator}} – Is used for planting crops and trees.
* {{Item link|Butcher Knife}} – Allows the player to butcher tamed animals without frightening them.
*{{Item link|Scythe}} – Used to harvest multiple crops at once.

=== Fishing===
*{{Item link|Fishing Rod}} – Is the intended way of obtaining fish.
*{{Item link|Fishing Bait}} – Is required for using the fishing rod.

===Logging ([[Axes]])===
*{{Item link|Stone Axe}} – Is a basic axe only capable of chopping down [[Beech]], [[Fir]] and [[Pine]] trees.
* {{Item link|Flint Axe}} – Chops the same trees as [[Stone Axe]], but does more damage and is more durable.
*{{Item link|Bronze Axe}} – Can chop down [[Ancient Tree|Ancient]], [[Birch]], and [[Oak]] trees, in addition to what previous axes can chop.
*{{Item link|Battleaxe}} – Is a two-handed axe that is slightly less powerful at chopping trees than [[Bronze Axe]]
* {{Item link|Iron Axe}} – Chops the same trees as [[Bronze Axe]], but does more damage and is more durable.
*{{Item link|Crystal Battleaxe}} – Is a two-handed axe that is slightly less powerful at chopping trees than [[Iron Axe]].
*{{Item link|Black Metal Axe}} – Can chop [[Yggdrasil Shoot|Yggdrasil]] trees, in addition to what previous axes can chop.
* {{Item link|Jotun Bane}} – Chops the same trees as [[Black Metal Axe]], but does more damage and is more durable.

===Mining ([[Pickaxes]])===
*{{Item link|Antler Pickaxe}} – Can mine [[Stone]], [[Copper Deposit|Copper]], [[Tin Deposit|Tin]], [[Muddy Scrap Pile]], [[Abyssal Barnacle]]
*{{Item link|Bronze Pickaxe}} – Can mine the same things as [[Antler Pickaxe]], but does more damage and is more durable.
*{{Item link|Iron Pickaxe}} – Can mine [[Obsidian Deposit|Obsidian]], [[Silver Vein|Silver]], [[Glowing metal]], in addition to what the previous pickaxes can.
*{{Item link|Black Metal Pickaxe}} – Can mine [[Black Marble]], [[Soft Tissue]] and [[Flametal Ore Vein|Flametal]] in addition to what the previous pickaxes can.

{{image link|Wooden atgeir|size=48px}}{{image link|Wooden greatsword|size=48px}} |} == Properties== ===Wielding (One-handed/Two-handed)=== Only '''one-handed weapons''' can be simultaneously equipped with [[shields]] or a [[Torch]]. All melee '''two-handed weapons''' have a greater movement speed reduction and cannot be used together with shields or a torch. ===[[Damage and Blocking Mechanics|Offensive and defensive properties]]=== ====Damage/Damage type==== All damages in ''[[Valheim]]'' have a '''damage type'''. Some [[creatures]] have weaknesses/resistances to certain [[damage types]], which increases/decreases the effectiveness of these damages. For example, [[Skeleton]]s are weak to blunt damage and resist pierce damage. When creatures are hit by damage with damage types they are weak/resist to, the damage numbers would be shown in yellow/grey color compared to the usual white color. Similar types of weapons mostly deal the same type of damage: *Blunt damage: One/two-handed [[Clubs]] *Slash damage: One/two-handed [[Axes]], [[Swords]] *Pierce damage: [[Spears]], [[Polearms]], [[Pickaxes]], [[Bows]] *Half slash, half pierce damage: [[Knives]] Exceptions include weapons that deal elemental damage like [[Torch]], [[Frostner]] and [[Draugr fang]]. Some [[clubs]] including [[Stagbreaker]] and [[Porcupine]] also deal pierce damage besides blunt damage. Keep in mind that not all damage types are upgraded when upgrading some weapons. ====Block armor and block force==== All weapons have a value of block armor, indicating the amount of damage absorbed when blocked by the weapon. Block force shows the amount of knockback applied to enemies when blocked. ====[[Parry|Parry and Parry bonus]]==== Weapons and shields, except tower [[shields]], can be used to parry attacks, with varying parry bonuses. Parry bonus is a multiplier to block armor (damage absorbed) when parrying. Damage dealt to the enemy in a period of time after a successful parry that absorbs all the damage is always 2x. Parry bonus is mostly determined by the weapon type: *Tower [[shields]]: Cannot parry *[[Tankard]], [[Bows]], Round [[shields]]: 1.5x *Buckler [[shields]]: 2.5x *[[Polearms]] (atgeirs): 3x *[[Knives]]: 4x *[[Flesh rippers]]: 6x *All other weapons: 2x ====Backstab==== Backstab indicates the multiplier applied to enemies when backstabbing. The backstab bonus is applied when attacking unaware enemies, regardless of whether they are facing towards or away from the player. Backstabbing an enemy gives it a backstab immunity for 5 minutes. Backstabbing can occur even if the enemy has partial HP. An enemy which has a red exclamation point over its name and HP bar, indicating that it is aware of your location, cannot be backstabbed. *[[Abyssal Harpoon]]: 1x *Two-handed [[clubs]]: 2x *[[Tankard]] (Cannot attack): 4x *[[Knives]] and [[Flesh rippers]]: 6x *All other weapons, including [[bows]] and one-handed [[clubs]]: 3x ====Knockback==== Knockback shows how far enemies are knocked back when attacked by the weapon. ===Movement speed=== Most weapons, when equipped, decrease the character's movement speed and increase dodge roll cost. The movement speed effect is mostly determined by the weapon type: *[[Flesh Rippers]] and [[Knives]]: -0% (No movement speed reduction) *All other one-handed melee weapons, [[Bows]], non-Tower [[Shields]], [[Pickaxes]], [[Polearms]], and [[Magic]]: -5% *[[Serpent Scale Shield]]: -15% *Two-handed [[Axes]], two-handed [[Clubs]], and [[Shields|Tower Shields]] other than [[Serpent Scale Shield]]: -20% == Melee weapons == Melee weapons are [[items]] that can be equipped to increase attack damage. Different types of melee weapon can have different ranges, attack speeds, stamina costs per attack and secondary attacks. When equipping one-handed weapons, the character can also equip [[shields]]. Most melee weapons' attack pattern involve a 3-hit combo. Generally, the first hit has the slowest delay (from the initial click), the second hit has less delay, and the third hit is slightly slower while dealing the most damage. Most melee weapons are quicker to recover and block from a miss than after a direct strike. Below are details regarding each type of melee weapon: === [[Axes]] === Axes are the only type of weapon that can be used to cut down trees. Though they can also be used against creatures, the lower slash damage compared to [[swords]] makes this inadvisable. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Axes}} |} === [[Clubs]] === Clubs primarily deal [[Damage types|blunt]] damage and feature high knockback. The knockback from clubs allows the player to keep enemies at arms' length and is sufficient to displace some enemies out of their effective attack range. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Clubs}} |} === [[Swords]] === Swords have low knockback and low stamina cost for good damage. Sword damage is not reduced when several enemies or objects are hit by a single attack, unlike most other weapons. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Swords}} |} === [[Spears]] === Spears have a fast attack with short range and low stamina cost. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Spears}} |} === [[Polearms]] === Polearms are strong two-handed weapons. All polearms deal pierce damage, and have a distinct AoE special attack. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Polearms}} |} === [[Knives]] === Knives have fast attacks with short range and low stamina cost. Knives deal 6x damage against unalerted enemies, whereas most other weapons do 3x. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Knives}} |} === [[Fists]] === When a player attacks without a weapon, tool equipped, or use a dedicated Fist weapon such as the [[Flesh Rippers]], they do a Fist strike. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Fists}} |} === [[Shields]] === Shields are weapons that can be used with other one-handed weapons. The block power, parry force and parry bonus of the weapons used with shields would be replaced by that of the shield used. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Shields}} |} == Ranged weapons == === [[Bows]] === Bows are weapons that shoot equipped arrows. Unlike melee weapons, attacks consume equipped [[arrows]] and can be charged while spending stamina to increase range and damage. Bows cannot be used when there are no arrows left in the inventory. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" ! rowspan="2" |{{:Bows}} |} === [[Crossbows]] === Crossbows are weapons that shoot equipped bolts. Like bows, attacks consume [[Bolts]]. Crossbows are slow to load, but have great damage and long range with no trajectory drop. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Crossbows}} |} == Magic weapons == Magic weapons need [[Eitr]] to be used. There are two types of magic weapons, [[Elemental magic]] and [[Blood magic]]. ===[[Elemental magic]] === {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Elemental magic}} |} === [[Blood magic]] === Blood magic weapons drain some of the caster's [[Health]] (''current'' health, ''not'' maximum health) per cast. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Blood magic}} |} == Ammunition == === [[Arrows]] === Arrows are items that can be shot by bows. Bows cannot be used without arrows. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Arrows}} |} === [[Bolts]] === Bolts are items that can be shot by crossbows. Crossbows cannot be used without bolts. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Bolts}} |} === [[Missiles]] === Missiles are items that can be shot by the [[Ballista]]. Ballistae cannot be armed without missiles. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Missiles}} |} === [[Bombs]] === Bombs are weapons that are thrown by the character and consumed when used. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Bombs}} |} === [[Blob Bombs]] === Blob bombs are a type of Bombs that summon a creature on impact. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Blob bombs}} |} == [[Wooden weapons]] == Wooden weapons is a series of weapons that deals only 1 damage. They are mainly suited for training and practice matches between players. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Wooden weapons}} |} == Achievements == {{Achievement|AllWeaponCraft}} {{Weapons}} [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Items]] [[uk:Зброя]] [[cs:Zbraně]] [[ru:Оружие]] [[fr:Arme]]

A '''Tree Stump''' is left after a [[Trees|tree]] is chopped down. It acts as a small source of [[Wood]]. Harvesting these stumps provide up to a maximum of 2 Wood.
[[File:Swing-At-Stump.png|alt=|left|thumb|'''The player swings at stump''']]
Like trees, stumps can also be ''"too hard"'', depending on the tier of the axe or pickaxe used.

Stumps can be damaged with both axes and pickaxes. A stump always drops two pieces of the tree's basic wood: {{Item link|Wood}} for most trees, {{Item link|Ashwood}} for [[Scorched Tree]]s and {{Item link|Timberwood}} for the pine-shaped [[Timber Tree]]s.

Old stumps that are not left by a felled tree also grow naturally in several biomes. They drop more wood than tree stumps.

'''Wisp Fountains''' are [[Player base|base]] structures used for collecting [[Wisp]]s, which will be attracted to the fountain when it is dark; either when it is night, or raining, in any biome. Torches and other artificial light sources do not prevent it from summoning wisps.  

They require a [[Stonecutter]] to be built.

== Notes ==
Wisps begin to appear around 18:00. They also appear when it is raining.

A new wisp will join the fountain every 30 seconds, with initially up to three wisps present at a time. Eventually, up to nine wisps can be present near morning.

Hovering over the fountain whilst it is dark enough to attract wisps, it will say, "The wisps are coming." Once the fountain has three wisps, the text will change to "The wisps are dancing." This seems to indicate the fountain has the maximum number of wisps circling it, but it is possible to have more, seemingly due to a bug or quirk in the way the wisp spawning works.

If the player has more than one fountain nearby, the maximum number of wisps is shared among them. Spread the fountains out by more than 20 meters to allow each to reach its maximum.

If they are not caught before the day comes, wisps will fly away and disappear. During the day, while hovering over the fountain, it will say, "The wisps demand darkness."

== Tips ==
* Wisps can also appear during the day if rainy or stormy weather conditions are active. Some players have observed that weather effects triggered by certain boss encounters (such as Eikthyr’s storm) can temporarily allow wisps to spawn even outside normal nighttime conditions, as long as the player remains within the affected area.

* Keeping strong wind active through weather events can also be useful for nearby wind-powered structures, such as windmills, allowing both wisp farming and production benefits at the same time.

* Because wisps will despawn once daylight returns and darkness conditions are no longer met, staying close to the source of the weather effect is required to maintain their appearance.

* In addition to nighttime, some biomes such as the Swamp provide permanent low-light environments, provided the area remains loaded by nearby players.


== Trivia ==
* The description of the Wisp Fountain is a reference to the Aliens movie. The character Newt says the line.

The '''Wisplight''' is an accessory made of [[Silver]] and [[Wisp]] at a [[Workbench]]. It is unlocked after acquiring a [[Wisp]] for the first time.

==Usage==
The light clears the [[Mist]] of [[Mistlands]] in a 15 meter radius around itself. The orb loosely follows the player and can briefly leave the player in a fog if they change direction too quickly.

It is equipped in the accessory slot, and thus allows players to wear a full set of armor in addition to the light. The Wisplight conflicts with the [[Megingjord]] and the [[Wishbone]], which occupy the same equipment slot.

==Notes==
*When equipped, the message "You release the bound wisp" will appear.
*The mist is also cleared by [[Wisp Torch]]es, the [[Mistwalker]], and some [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]] structures.
**Using the Mistwalker to clear the mist allows you to temporarily wear the Megingjord to transport [[Scrap Iron|Iron]] and [[Copper Scrap]]. Its range is much less than the Wisplight, so this tactic should not be used unless the extra carry weight is needed.

== Trivia ==
* Before the [[1.0]] update, the Wisplight used to clear the mist in only a 10 meter radius.

'''Chain lightning''' is an on-hit effect triggered by weapons upgraded with [[Iolite]] or [[Thunderblood Essence]].

==Effect==
Chain lightning has a 25% chance to trigger on a normal attack and a 20% chance to trigger on a secondary attack.

It deals 75 [[lightning]] damage to the target, the amount is not affected by skills, and it cannot be blocked or dodged.

Once triggered, it has an 80% chance of bouncing off nearby enemies or players. If so, each nearby target within 8 meters has a 30% chance of being targeted, up to a maximum of 2–4 targets per bounce (the maximum is chosen at random then targets are processed starting from the nearest). The process repeats indefinitely, centered on each new target, but with the chance of rebound multiplied by 0.75 each time (i.e., 80% → 60% → 45% → 33.75%, etc.).

A single activation of chain lightning cannot affect the same target more than once.

==Notes==
* Chain lightning within the vicinity of neutral [[Ashlands Dvergr]] has the potential of damaging them, immediately turning them hostile.
